item.title: How should you interpret a survey rating that combines speed and quality?
item.description: A single rating for response speed and resolution quality hides which one needs attention. Learn how to split the question, test its meaning, retain a useful overall measure and handle trend breaks.

item.title: An editable review page is a transaction-state problem, not a navigation problem
item.description: An editable review must preserve the same task, recalculate invalidated answers and separate final submission from browser history, refreshes and retries.

item.title: Cookie Path Narrows Sending Scope; It Does Not Isolate Same-Origin Permissions
item.description: Cookie Path determines which requests carry a value, not authorization or same-origin isolation. Learn the matching rules, duplicate-name risk, migration cleanup, and server-side checks.

item.title: Why doesn't Docker restart an unhealthy container?
item.description: Docker HEALTHCHECK records a health state, while restart policies act on container lifecycle events. Learn the boundary, Compose startup dependencies, and a verifiable recovery design.

item.title: Which Changes Should Stop When the Error Budget Is Exhausted?
item.description: An error budget is a written contract between measurement and change decisions. Verify scope and causes, restrict higher-risk actions, and define exceptions, approvers, and evidence for lifting restrictions.

item.title: Tie Each Form Answer to a Service Decision
item.description: A field protocol names who uses an answer, which decision it changes, which users need to provide it, and how it is validated, retained, and deleted. A clear label is not a reason to collect data.

item.title: A Path Is Still Tracked After .gitignore: Separate Rules, Index, and Worktree
item.description: A .gitignore rule applies to untracked paths. Check the index and worktree separately before choosing whether to untrack a file, keep local configuration, or respond to an exposed secret.

item.title: Accept Is a Preference, Not a Guarantee: How to Check the Actual HTTP Response
item.description: Accept states a client's preferred representations; status, Content-Type, body syntax, and business structure still need separate checks, and 406 is not mandatory.

item.title: Why can a decompressed body differ from Content-Length?
item.description: Response headers report octets at a representation layer; content coding, HTTP/1.1 framing, and JavaScript string length are different quantities.

item.title: Preserve long identifiers before numeric parsing loses precision
item.description: JSON number syntax can be valid while a long identifier loses distinguishable digits. Preserve identity before conversion and verify every boundary.

item.title: Always Still Downloads Very Little: Which Image Is the Node Running?
item.description: imagePullPolicy: Always resolves a reference again while reusing cached layers. Check the Pod template, runtime imageID, and rollout to verify a release.

item.title: The Button Is Transparent, but Tab Still Finds It: Hiding Must Change Three Paths
item.description: opacity: 0 changes visual compositing, not pointer targeting or keyboard focus. Choose the actual state mechanism for a control, subtree, or transition, and check assistive-technology exposure separately.

item.title: Why Is a Span Still Unset After Recording an Exception? Judge the Operation First
item.description: `recordException` adds an exception event; it does not set Span status to Error. Use the Span’s operation boundary, final outcome, and applicable semantic conventions to decide which signals to record.

item.title: In Playwright, Wait for the User Task, Not Network Silence
item.description: networkidle reports a brief lack of connections, not rendered results or task success. Choose between URL, control, business-outcome, and network assertions based on the test contract.

item.title: Why Does numeric(4,2) Round Extra Places but Reject 99.995?
item.description: PostgreSQL numeric(p,s) rounds to its declared scale before checking integer capacity. Storage rounding is not input validation; distinguish two rejection policies before conversion.

item.title: A PostgreSQL Sequence Gap Does Not Prove a Lost Record
item.description: Rollback, ON CONFLICT, and sequence caching can leave gaps. Diagnose them against committed rows and business state; do not treat a primary key as a completion counter.

item.title: A Prometheus Recording Rule Returned a Value—Why Did the Instance Label Disappear?
item.description: A recording rule writes a new series. Aggregation, vector matching and label overrides can change its identity. Trace the expression, rule group and downstream queries.

item.title: The Save Succeeded, but finally Rejected: What Should the Caller Retry?
item.description: A rejected finally cleanup changes the returned chain, but says nothing by itself about whether an external write committed. Separate operation, cleanup, and retry state.

item.title: An xfail Test Started Passing—Why Can CI Still Stay Green?
item.description: By default, XPASS is reported but need not fail the suite. Strictness changes the gate, not assertion validity; check configuration against the pytest version and retain removal evidence.

item.title: Validate redirect destinations as a navigation trust boundary
item.description: Prefer server-side destination mappings; when URLs are necessary, validate parsed components and keep navigation policy separate from authorization.

item.title: Understand per-tab storage without assuming a blank initial state
item.description: sessionStorage is usually isolated by origin and page session, but a new auxiliary context with an opener can start from a copy. Use task identity to distinguish fresh work from recovery.

item.title: Bound retries after a rate-limit response
item.description: A 429 signals rate limiting but does not choose a retry count. Combine Retry-After with replay safety, cancellation and an overall deadline to define bounded attempts and clear terminal states.

item.title: A contract table for PUT and PATCH updates
item.description: PUT uses a request representation to define target state; PATCH applies instructions in a specified format. The contract table covers omissions, nulls, arrays, and stale versions, while concurrency and domain commands need separate rules.

item.title: The npm audit report is green after --force. Is it ready to ship?
item.description: npm audit fix --force may cross declared dependency ranges. Learn how to connect the report, lockfile, compatibility checks, and release artifact before shipping.

item.title: Why does a mounted volume still show old files after an image update?
item.description: Docker copies destination files into an empty volume on its initial mount by default; an existing volume then obscures newer image files. Learn how to inspect mounts, plan migrations, and preserve safe rollback.

item.title: A stale flag is not an off switch: separate three layers before retirement
item.description: A lifecycle label is a cleanup signal, not proof that runtime behavior or source branches have changed. Follow a hypothetical rollout to retire a flag in dependency order, including consumer and rollback checks.

item.title: Git bisect can narrow the range and still leave the culprit uncertain
item.description: A bisect result depends on a consistent property predicate. Separate setup errors, behavior regressions, and skipped revisions before interpreting a boundary or making a causal claim.

item.title: Git revert records an inverse commit; how do you verify recovery?
item.description: A revert preserves the original and records an inverse change. Verify the tree, merge parent, built artifact, and runtime separately to state what actually recovered.

item.title: Can an old IndexedDB transaction still write after `await fetch()`? Check its state
item.description: After IndexedDB requests are handled and control returns to the event loop, an old transaction may auto-commit; keep network waits before the short local write transaction.

item.title: Why does `sort()` change the original array?
item.description: `sort()` mutates its array and returns the same reference; copying the container does not isolate its record objects.

item.title: Does a CronJob creating a Job guarantee the business runs only once?
item.description: A CronJob does not guarantee exactly-once business execution. Separate schedule slots, Job attempts, and business periods; use stable business keys and durable outcome records to make retries converge and recover.

item.title: Does a TraceId in a log guarantee a complete trace?
item.description: A TraceId is correlation identity, not a receipt that spans were collected, exported, retained, or visible to the current account. Check context, sampling, export, query scope, and authorization separately.

item.title: What makes this the representative row in each group?
item.description: PostgreSQL DISTINCT ON keeps the first ordered row in each group. Separate eligibility, business precedence, tie-breaking, and presentation order to explain why that row represents the group.

item.title: Why did NOT IN omit the rows I expected to be unmatched?
item.description: A right-side NULL, an empty subquery, and a NULL left value produce different three-valued outcomes for NOT IN. Define what unknown identity means before rewriting to NOT EXISTS or relying on constraints.

item.title: Why did PostgreSQL ignore the offset in my timestamp string?
item.description: PostgreSQL interprets an offset-bearing string according to its type: timestamp without time zone keeps calendar fields and ignores the offset, while timestamptz represents an instant. This guide distinguishes typed literals, session TimeZone, both AT TIME ZONE directions, DST am

item.title: How to tell zero values, missing targets, and failed scrapes apart in Prometheus
item.description: An empty PromQL vector is not a measured zero. Use query time, up, target inventory, and absent functions to separate inactivity, scrape failure, and a missing target.

item.title: Field or lab user research? Start with the question you need answered
item.description: Field and lab studies answer different questions. Choose a setting for context discovery, interface comparison, or service-in-use evidence, then separate observation from interpretation.

item.title: Why does a CDN script with integrity still fail to load? Separate hash and CORS failures
item.description: A cross-origin script with integrity can still be rejected. Check request mode, CORS headers, final response bytes, and the digest separately, then define a bounded fallback.

item.title: A monkeypatch restores a function reference, not everything the test already did
item.description: pytest restores managed replacements at the end of a test or fixture. Threads, started subprocesses, cached configuration, and external side effects need their own boundaries and cleanup.

item.title: Fixed dates, fast-forward, and ticking clocks test different behavior
item.description: Playwright's fixed-date, fast-forward, ticking, and system-time controls produce different callback behavior. Define the time semantics first, then choose an API and assert the product outcome.

item.title: Define the base and reference before composing an API URL
item.description: The URL constructor resolves references by path rules; a trailing slash, root-relative input, and an absolute input produce different destinations.

item.title: Why Is a Required Check Still Waiting After Path Filtering?
item.description: A GitHub Actions paths filter can prevent a workflow run from being created, leaving a required check pending. Keep the gate observable while selecting affected tests inside the workflow.

item.title: Should a CSP nonce follow the build or the response?
item.description: Generate a CSP nonce with each policy response and keep headers and approved tags aligned; evaluate content hashes for static scripts.

item.title: Make the container entrypoint hand off signals deliberately
item.description: Trace the container's main process and signal recipient before evaluating wrapper behavior, application shutdown, and orchestrator grace periods.

item.title: Treat a download filename as a suggestion, not a local path
item.description: Treat Content-Disposition as a display hint: choose the write directory, storage identity, and permitted content type independently, then validate decoding and path containment.

item.title: A successful HEAD response does not verify the GET body
item.description: HEAD success proves only that the method request succeeded; verify the GET representation under matching identity and negotiation conditions to check its body and locale.

item.title: Who sets priority and accepts handoff during an incident?
item.description: Separate incident command, system operations, communications, and planning as explicit responsibilities; coordinate parallel response with a live state and acknowledged handoff.

item.title: What Can Still Happen After You Configure a PDB?
item.description: A PodDisruptionBudget constrains voluntary evictions through the Eviction API. Node failures, direct deletion, and controller rollouts have different boundaries.

item.title: Network Chunks Split Chinese Characters: Where Should You Handle It?
item.description: Preserve split UTF-8 characters with a stateful decoder, then frame messages by protocol; correct decoding still does not complete a record.

item.title: Respect writable backpressure before sending more chunks
item.description: When write() returns false, stop initiating writes and resume on drain; it signals buffer pressure, not rejection or business completion.

item.title: Delta is not more fragile than Cumulative: decide where conversion state lives
item.description: Delta covers adjacent intervals; Cumulative covers a shared start through now. Choose by where state, gaps, and restart handling belong.

item.title: Does changing a password sign out other devices? Verify server-side revocation
item.description: Password updates do not prove other sessions are revoked. Distinguish routine reset from suspected compromise and verify server-side rejection.

item.title: When should a Playwright test use first() after matching two buttons?
item.description: A strictness error means a single-target action has no unique identity. Anchor the button to its record; use an ordered choice only when the requirement names that order.

item.title: When does a PostgreSQL advisory lock release through a connection pool?
item.description: A session advisory lock ends on explicit release or backend-session termination, not on rollback or pool release. Choose transaction scope or pinned-session ownership and test the actual pool mode.

item.title: Rate each Prometheus counter before aggregation: why reset identity matters
item.description: Calculate counter rates per original series before aggregation so an instance restart is not hidden by other replicas. The guide also covers rate extrapolation, label changes, gauges and histogram ratios.

item.title: Should prototype code be rewritten? Start with its real side effects
item.description: Use a hypothetical refund flow to separate prototype evidence from production proof: verify identity, durable state, duplicate requests, recovery, and ownership before deciding what to reuse.

item.title: Why pytest parameter cases contaminate each other: trace shared objects before copying
item.description: pytest passes parameter values as-is. Trace list identity, nested references, and expectations before choosing fresh construction, a fixture, or copying.

item.title: useId Is Not a Universal Key: Separate DOM Links, Data Identity, and Hydration Trees
item.description: Use React useId for accessibility relationships. List keys come from data, hydration requires matching trees, and multiple roots need coordinated identifierPrefix values.

item.title: Do Not Write an Action as Its Cause: Use Competing Explanations to Choose the Next Research Step
item.description: A user returning to the previous page is an observation, not proof that a form is confusing. Separate behavior, cause hypotheses and actions, then choose research that can distinguish them.

item.title: A SQLite foreign key in the schema does not protect every connection
item.description: SQLite stores foreign-key declarations in the schema, but enforcement is a connection setting. Initialize and read back each connection, then verify writes and inspect existing data.

item.title: Why can 400% zoom still hide content after mobile passes?
item.description: A mobile screenshot does not verify zoom reflow. Check content and tasks at a 320 CSS pixel viewport, and keep two-dimensional exceptions local.

item.title: A verified signature can still leave the review approval on the wrong revision
item.description: Verified means the platform validated a commit signature. It does not show that a reviewer approved the current diff. Bind review, checks, artifacts and deployment to exact revisions.

item.title: Why does a process keep old settings after a ConfigMap update?
item.description: After a ConfigMap update, a process may still use old settings. Trace environment variables, projected volumes, subPath mounts, application reload, and each replica’s effective revision.

item.title: Can you retry after a CORS error? First find out whether the operation ran
item.description: A browser CORS error alone cannot prove that the server did nothing. Separate a rejected preflight from an unreadable response or transport failure, then use the server's operation record to decide whether retry is safe.

item.title: What does the server receive after a POST redirect? Inspect each hop
item.description: After a POST receives a 3xx response, the destination's request depends on the status and client. Inspect method, body, credentials, and side effects at every hop.

item.title: Why can one URL return the wrong language from cache? Treat Vary as a contract
item.description: One URL can select different representations from request headers. Use Vary to state reuse conditions, then verify defaults, private responses, and proxy cache policy separately.

item.title: Why can a successful page flow still leave users stuck at a handoff?
item.description: Define cross-team handoffs through explicit states, usable evidence, acceptance and ownership transfer so page success is not mistaken for task completion.

item.title: Why can tests with high coverage miss a wrong comparison operator?
item.description: Use a surviving >= to > mutant to inspect input boundaries, test oracles and mutant validity; treat the score as a review signal, not proof of test adequacy.

item.title: Why can two builds differ even when npm ci locks the dependencies?
item.description: npm ci constrains dependency installation, not every build input. Inventory runtime, platform, configuration and time, then define how artifacts are compared.

item.title: Why can PostgreSQL save NULL when a CHECK says greater than zero?
item.description: PostgreSQL treats TRUE and NULL as satisfying CHECK. Define value ranges, required states and historical-data migrations separately; do not turn unknown into zero.

item.title: Why Can the Application Still Read Every Tenant with RLS Policies in Place?
item.description: RLS behavior depends on more than policy text: runtime roles, table ownership, policy composition, and tenant context all affect access.

item.title: An empty SKIP LOCKED result is not an empty queue
item.description: An empty SKIP LOCKED claim means this statement acquired no eligible row; track pending, claimed, completed, and recoverable work separately.

item.title: Why is the database file still large after VACUUM?
item.description: Ordinary VACUUM mainly makes space reusable; shrinking a file is a different rewrite outcome with lock, temporary-disk, and workload costs.

item.title: Aggregate distributions before estimating a fleet quantile
item.description: The arithmetic mean of instance P95s is not the request population's P95. Define the population, aggregate histogram distributions, and check summaries, bucket boundaries, and estimation error.

item.title: Property tests still need an independent behavioral claim
item.description: Generated inputs widen exploration, but they do not define correctness. Review the contract, oracle, boundaries and mutations that challenge each assertion.

item.title: Why does React show the old filtered list before updating again?
item.description: When a list and its filter already determine the screen, do not store another result with an Effect. Separate stale renders, independent drafts, performance caches, and external synchronization.

item.title: If Motion Stops, Is the Upload Still Running? Separate State from Animation
item.description: Use an upload flow to separate business state, visible feedback, and assistive-technology announcements when reducing motion.

item.title: Why Can a Regex Validator Stall a Service?
item.description: Regex validation needs an enforceable resource budget. Learn how backtracking cost, input bounds, engine tradeoffs and interruptible timeouts fit together.

item.title: Does Interview Consent Let You Send the Recording to Any Tool?
item.description: Interview consent is not a pass for every tool. Trace purpose, recipients, vendor processing and derived copies so a team can review an upload and locate the material affected by a withdrawal.

item.title: Transferring a buffer changes ownership rather than making a second copy
item.description: A transfer does not create another usable copy: it gives an ArrayBuffer to the result or receiver. Understand reachability, synchronous detachment and asynchronous retries before treating the original buffer as a backup.

item.title: Verify webhook signatures before changing the request body
item.description: Stripe verification depends on the original request body, signature header, and endpoint secret. Trace middleware, retries, and deduplication when equal-looking JSON fails, while keeping other providers' protocol boundaries clear.

item.title: With GitHub Actions OIDC, whom should an AWS production role trust?
item.description: After GitHub Actions exchanges OIDC for temporary AWS credentials, teams still need to constrain token requests, role trust claims, and role permissions. This guide explains subject-format changes, Environment branch conditions, and denial paths.

item.title: Prometheus for keeps restarting when each value creates a new alert identity
item.description: Trace changing value labels through pending, move display measurements into annotations, and separate rule timers from Alertmanager grouping.

item.title: A completed Deployment rollout still needs user-path acceptance
item.description: A completed Deployment rollout proves controller-observed conditions, not user success. Separate revision identity, Pod readiness, business-path acceptance, and rollback signals.

item.title: How can an uncommitted local file enter a Docker build context?
item.description: Local directories, remote Git sources, and named contexts have different input boundaries. Inspect the build arguments, effective ignore rules, and image separately.

item.title: What must the server verify after browser validation passes?
item.description: Browser feedback cannot authorize a target object or reserve changing business state; the API must independently check the request, caller, and write-time conditions.

item.title: Why downstream work can survive an upstream timeout
item.description: A timeout ends a waiting window; it does not kill arbitrary background work. Propagate remaining budgets and cancellation to executors, then handle committed side effects separately.

item.title: How can a resumed download avoid joining two file versions?
item.description: A byte offset does not identify a file version. Use If-Range to condition resumption, validate Content-Range on 206, and route a full 200 response through replacement.

item.title: A valid JWT signature does not establish the intended recipient
item.description: Signature verification answers a cryptographic question, not who should accept a token. RFC 7519, RFC 8725, and the OAuth JWT access-token profile explain audience validation and its limits.

item.title: Password-hash upgrades are constrained by what the old hash cannot reveal
item.description: Compare login-time rehashing, dormant-account recovery, weak legacy hashes, concurrent password changes, and rollback as one verifiable migration plan.

item.title: A completed click still does not prove that a save succeeded
item.description: Playwright waits for click actionability and an initiated navigation, but the application must define when saving is complete. Choose a rereadable outcome and distinguish acceptance, persistence, and failure.

item.title: Intl.PluralRules Selects Categories, Not Sentences
item.description: Plural categories are neither translations nor product empty states. Separate complete messages, zero semantics, number formatting, and runtime tests.

item.title: `clock_timestamp()` Is Not a Commit Timestamp in PostgreSQL 19
item.description: `clock_timestamp()` records when it is evaluated, not when a transaction commits. Choose a time source for transaction, command, observation, or commit events, and understand commit tracking's limits.

item.title: Use a lifecycle map to choose PostgreSQL ON DELETE
item.description: Use order lines, a shared catalog and historical snapshots to choose CASCADE, RESTRICT, NO ACTION or SET NULL, then verify the deletion scope.

item.title: How can PostgreSQL imports report results after per-row savepoints?
item.description: A SAVEPOINT rolls back part of a transaction; it does not commit each row. A trustworthy partial-import receipt needs stable input identities and a queryable outcome tied to the outer commit boundary.

item.title: How can you verify an incident action without overstating risk reduction?
item.description: Turn postmortem actions into falsifiable acceptance checks, distinguishing a closed task, a tested scenario, and a longer-term change in risk.

item.title: Why Do Tests Start Affecting One Another After a Fixture Scope Change?
item.description: pytest fixture scope extends reuse and state lifetime, not isolation. Decide from mutability, cleanup boundaries, dependency scope, and external resource identity.

item.title: When Is Discovery Finished? When the Next Decision Is Defensible
item.description: Discovery should not end because a quota of interviews or prototypes was met. Put problem evidence, alternatives, hard constraints, and decisive unknowns on one decision map before choosing to proceed, stop, or narrow the next test.

item.title: HTTP 202 Acknowledges Processing, Not a Completed Business Result
item.description: HTTP 202 acknowledges acceptance for processing. An async API must also define durable acceptance, terminal-state retrieval, result authorization, and recovery from uncertainty.

item.title: Why Readable HTTP Errors Still Leave Clients Unable to Act
item.description: Readable error text is not a stable client contract. RFC 9457 separates problem identity, occurrence detail, and HTTP status; learn when a client can correct, wait, stop, or fall back safely.

item.title: Why Research with Familiar Users Misses Important Journeys
item.description: Familiar users can explain familiar paths, but not always why newcomers never enter them. Match research questions, task conditions, and recruitment channels, then bound conclusions to the evidence actually covered.

item.title: How Can You Prove a Downloaded Build Is the One Approved?
item.description: A successful download and matching digest prove only part of an artifact handoff. Track source, workflow run, digest, provenance and approval separately so deployment cannot select a different build by name.

item.title: Should You Edit or Supersede an Old ADR? Check Whether It Reached Implementation
item.description: Choose how to revise an ADR based on its status, implementation history, and whether a replacement has been accepted. Preserve traceable history without implying that supersession completes migration.

item.title: Zero CSP Reports Are Not a Green Light to Block: Verify Three Things First
item.description: Zero CSP reports do not prove enforcement is ready. Verify response headers, report collection and critical workflows, then block in a bounded, reversible scope.

item.title: After Setting SameSite, Which CSRF Paths Still Need Verification?
item.description: SameSite restricts some cross-site cookie delivery. Review write routes, request methods, origins, tokens and resulting state instead of treating one attribute as CSRF acceptance.

item.title: A Docker Secret Mount Protects Delivery, Not Every Build Output
item.description: A Docker secret mount limits how a credential is delivered, not what the consuming command can write. Inspect outputs and remember that rotating the value alone does not invalidate a RUN cache.

item.title: Why Should a Log Field Allowlist Come Before Collector Redaction?
item.description: Define log events around the action, authorization decision and write outcome an investigation needs, then inspect fields in collectors, indexes and backups. Downstream redaction cannot prove upstream copies never existed.

item.title: The dialog closed, but where should focus go next?
item.description: Focus normally returns to the control that opened a modal. If a successful action removes that control, move focus to a logical place that continues the task, and verify cancel, success and failure separately.

item.title: Does readOnly automatically reject writes? OpenAPI 3.2.1 allows two choices
item.description: readOnly is a directional annotation, not a general write barrier. A server may ignore the submitted value or reject the request; the application still needs explicit mappings, permissions and observable outcomes.

item.title: Tail sampling cannot recover traces already discarded upstream
item.description: Tail sampling can judge only spans a Collector receives. Follow SDK drops, routing, late arrivals and buffer eviction to locate where an error trace became incomplete.

item.title: Row locks can still deadlock: why competing writers need one lock order
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 detects and breaks deadlock cycles, but cannot make the business operation succeed. Learn to order multi-resource locks, identify 40P01 and retry safely at the transaction boundary.

item.title: A JSONB GIN index does not support every query shape
item.description: In PostgreSQL 18, JSONB GIN support depends on the operator class, indexed expression and data distribution. Compare key-existence, containment and path queries before diagnosing the plan.

item.title: Pagination needs a unique order and a cross-page consistency policy
item.description: Use a unique order for PostgreSQL pagination, and define what concurrent changes may do between pages.

item.title: Why can a unique column still contain multiple NULLs?
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 treats NULLs as distinct in unique constraints by default. Choose NULLS NOT DISTINCT, NOT NULL, or a partial unique index from the business meaning of absence.

item.title: More clicks, fewer completed tasks? Define the denominator first
item.description: Define the user benefit, business unit, denominator, outcome states, and observation window before treating a rise in clicks or funnel conversion as task success.

item.title: Can one metric label per order make monitoring behave like an event database?
item.description: In Prometheus, label-value combinations identify time series. Before adding unbounded order dimensions, estimate the combination ceiling, inspect histogram behavior, and validate observed series growth.

item.title: Promise.all rejection does not cancel the remaining work
item.description: Promise.all rejects its aggregate on the first input failure but does not stop the inputs. Use AbortController for signal-aware reads and business-state rules for writes.

item.title: Terraform State Locking Does Not Freeze Cloud Resources
item.description: Terraform locks coordinate writes to one supported state backend; they cannot stop console, script, or separate-state changes to cloud resources.

item.title: Can a Timestamp with an Offset Express Nine Every Morning?
item.description: An offset timestamp identifies an instant. A recurring local 9 a.m. schedule also needs a recurrence rule, named time zone, ambiguity policy, and rule-update policy.

item.title: Image uploads need more than extension and MIME checks
item.description: Extensions, MIME and signatures are limited signals. A safer upload flow constrains parsing, quarantines unverified objects, binds review to a content version, and reauthorizes retrieval.

item.title: A smooth demo does not prove usability: write tasks without giving the answer
item.description: State the business goal, necessary materials, correct outcome and observation plan without giving the interface route; distinguish independent completion from moderator help, recovery and uncovered conditions.

item.title: Why a GitHub Actions Cache Hit Does Not Make a Release Trustworthy
item.description: A cache hit restores data; it does not establish cache provenance, lockfile installation, or release-artifact identity. Separate those checks using GitHub Actions cache scopes, cache-mode, and npm ci.

item.title: Why Can an Old Run Still Overwrite a Test Site When Branches Use Separate Locks?
item.description: GitHub Actions concurrency groups coordinate only same-named runs in a repository. Map the group to shared environments, then distinguish pending replacement, cancellation, and queue:max semantics.

item.title: How Are GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions Calculated for a Job with Workflow-Level Permissions?
item.description: Trace GITHUB_TOKEN permissions from organization or repository defaults through workflow and job declarations to event policies. Actions in the same job share that permission boundary.

item.title: Both Saves Succeeded: Why Did One Editor Lose Their Changes?
item.description: Use If-Match to reject stale writes, then connect strong ETags and atomic updates to a conflict flow that preserves the user's draft.

item.title: Can a Timed-Out Request Be Retried? Define the Business Idempotency Boundary
item.description: Handle an unknown timeout outcome by separating HTTP idempotence, stable intent keys, durable deduplication, and external side effects.

item.title: Search Results Went Backward: Cancellation Also Needs a State-Commit Guard
item.description: Prevent out-of-order search responses from rewriting the current view: cancel obsolete work, identify the active intent, and guard result, error, and loading updates.

item.title: Why Can no-cache Still Leave Cached Files?
item.description: no-cache permits storage but requires validation before reuse. Trace browser, proxy, and CDN evidence, then choose no-store and private deliberately.

item.title: A UUID Is Not an Authorization Decision: Four Checks for Every Order Request
item.description: UUIDs make enumeration harder but do not prove access rights. Model authorization across actions, tenants, asynchronous work, and static resources, then verify it with a controlled two-principal matrix.

item.title: A User Says ‘I’d Use It’: Reconstruct the Last Task Before Committing
item.description: An ‘I’d use it’ answer is a follow-up signal, not proof of demand or product effectiveness. Trace a recent task, separate recall from observation and inference, then choose the next research step.

item.title: Database Slowness Restarts Every Pod? Match Each Probe to Its Action
item.description: Kubernetes liveness failures restart containers, readiness failures make Pods temporarily ineligible for Service traffic, and startup probes protect initialization. Choose by failure location and recovery action instead of turning a shared dependency outage into a restart storm.

item.title: The Node Is Idle: Why Is the Container Still Slow?
item.description: Low average node CPU does not mean a container is free from its own CPU limit. Align request latency, container usage, throttling, requests, and memory events on one timeline before tuning.

item.title: preStop Is Configured but Requests Still Fail: Budget the Whole Shutdown
item.description: preStop is not extra grace time. Put hook execution, traffic withdrawal, in-flight work, and process cleanup inside one termination budget.

item.title: Why Should Customer Email Not Go Straight into OpenTelemetry Baggage?
item.description: Baggage is designed to propagate request context; the risk comes from the same mechanism. Separate propagation, telemetry storage, trust boundaries, and personal identifiers.

item.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY Is Still Waiting: What Should a Release Check?
item.description: Concurrent index builds avoid blocking ordinary writes, but still scan, wait on transactions and leave failure states. Read the phase, then verify validity and query behavior.
